items.title: A larger AI model hand-edited a smaller one's weights, with mixed results
items.why: GPT-6 Astra changed just 1,023 of Qwen's weights and nearly 5x'd its math score, but 6 of 16 edit runs got reverted as unreliable.
items.source: arXiv preprint (Shanghai AI Lab, Tongji & Fudan Universities)

items.title: Talk to a 3D-printed robot arm, and an AI agent moves it for you
items.why: An OpenClaw plugin gives an AI nine arm commands on a $30 CyberBrick ESP32 kit - a weekend build with its real debugging logged in public.

items.title: Seven $4 microcontrollers team up to run one tiny language model
items.why: A maker split a 0.4B-parameter 1.58-bit model across 7 ESP32-S3 boards over SPI - a template for distributed inference on scrap hardware.

items.title: A thumbnail upload can quietly take over the server that resizes it
items.why: A Ghostscript font-loading bug lets photo.jpg smuggle in PostScript that disables safety checks and runs commands as the renderer.

items.title: A fix for the one thing classic union-find couldn't do: delete fast
items.why: A new structure deletes from union-find in true constant time, closing a gap every prior version left open - handy for contest twists.

items.title: Coach yourself by name, not 'I', right before a tough question lands
items.why: A Michigan study: third-person self-talk cut panic and rated as better performance than first-person talk, with zero extra mental effort.
items.source: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (Kross & Moser, Univ. of Michigan)

items.title: Sound timed to your brain's sleep waves boosted its waste-clearing flow
items.why: MIT: pink-noise bursts synced to slow sleep waves raised fluid clearance in the brain - early, only 14 people, no memory benefit shown yet.

items.title: Six months of cardio training nudged a biological-age marker down
items.why: Small pilot (n=38): bigger VO2 max gains lined up with lower GrimAge scores - a lead on cardio's payoff, not yet a controlled proof.

items.title: Postgres stopped storing computed columns on disk by default
items.why: Generated columns now compute on read, not write - saves storage and write time, costs read CPU. Know the tradeoff before you pick one.

items.title: Four bpftrace one-liners that show exactly where your latency hides
items.why: Skip guessing from CPU graphs - attach a one-line eBPF probe to the exact syscall or I/O path you suspect for a live latency histogram.
